faqs.question: Are there really sugar-free Diwali sweets?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the sweet has no added sugar: no white sugar, jaggery, honey or palm sugar, which India's ICMR-INDIAB survey counts as added sugar. Sweets built on nuts, paneer or makhana and sweetened with a few dates or a non-nutritive sweetener qualify, though dates still carry their own fruit sugar.

faqs.question: Is jaggery a sugar-free option for Diwali sweets?
faqs.answer: No. The ICMR-INDIAB-21 analysis published in Nature Medicine in 2025 counts jaggery as added sugar alongside white sugar, honey and palm sugar. A gur laddoo is a traditional sweet, not a sugar-free one.

faqs.question: Can a person with diabetes eat sugar-free mithai at Diwali?
faqs.answer: Often in small portions, but that is a question for their own doctor, and nothing here is medical advice. India's RSSDI-ESI 2020 recommendations say artificial sweeteners may be consumed in recommended amounts and name festivals as a reason for regular glucose monitoring.

faqs.question: Does sucralose raise blood sugar?
faqs.answer: In a 12-week Indian trial of 210 adults with type 2 diabetes, replacing about 60 kcal of sugar in tea or coffee with sucralose did not change HbA1c or fasting glucose. It did bring a small drop of 0.5 kg in weight. That trial tested beverages, not mithai.

faqs.question: What does WHO say about sugar substitutes?
faqs.answer: WHO's guideline of 15 May 2023 conditionally recommends against non-sugar sweeteners for weight control. It does not apply to people with pre-existing diabetes and does not cover polyols such as sorbitol.

faqs.question: What warnings must a sugar-free sweet box carry in India?
faqs.answer: Under FSSAI's labelling rules, a package with an artificial sweetener must name it and carry warnings such as "Not recommended for children" for saccharin, with extra lines for aspartame and acesulfame potassium. Foods with 10% or more polyols must say they may have a laxative effect.

faqs.question: Can children eat sugar-free sweets?
faqs.answer: FSSAI's own label warnings say products with saccharin, acesulfame potassium or aspartame are not recommended for children, and sorbitol at 10% or more may cause bloating and diarrhoea in children. For a child, ask their doctor before offering a sweetener-based box.

faqs.question: Is ragi or millet mithai healthier for diabetes?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. ICMR-INDIAB-21 found that swapping refined cereals for whole wheat or millet flour without reducing total carbohydrate was not linked to lower diabetes risk. Portion size still decides most of the effect.

faqs.question: How much sugar is too much during Diwali week?
faqs.answer: ICMR-NIN's Dietary Guidelines for Indians set added sugar for adults at under 5% of total daily energy. Diwali 2027 runs five days, 27 to 31 October, so plan servings for the whole week with your doctor rather than day by day.

faqs.question: What can I send instead of sweets to someone avoiding sugar?
faqs.answer: A visit, a savoury box or a greeting works. SubhSandesh's Happy Diwali card ends with a drawn box of mithai and a Shubh Deepavali card signed by you, and 48.3% of SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Sugar-Free Diwali Sweets: Swaps, Label Warnings and the Evidence

Sugar-free Diwali sweets work best when the base is nuts, paneer, makhana or millet and the sweetness comes from a few dates or figs or a measured non-nutritive sweetener, not from jaggery or honey, which Indian surveys count as added sugar. This is not medical advice: if you or the person you are cooking for has diabetes, check with your doctor before Diwali on Friday 29 October 2027.

Two SubhSandesh numbers shape the last section. 48.3% of the pages people share on SubhSandesh are opened on a phone, and each page is viewed 11.1 times on average, so a greeting can carry some of the sweetness a sugar-free box cannot. Below are five original recipes, a sweetener table, the FSSAI label warnings, an Indian sucralose trial and a five-day plan.

## What makes a Diwali sweet "sugar-free" by Indian guidelines?

A sugar-free Diwali sweet has no added sugar, and in India's largest diet survey "added sugar" means white sugar, honey, jaggery and palm sugar added during cooking or at the table. That definition comes from the [ICMR-INDIAB survey-21 dietary analysis](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12618255) of 18,090 adults, published in Nature Medicine in September 2025. So a gur laddoo is not sugar-free, however traditional it is.

The same study found median added sugar intake ranged from 2.1% of daily energy in the Northeast to 7.9% in the North, with Haryana, Delhi, Karnataka, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh above 10%. The [ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians booklet](https://www.nin.res.in/downloads/DGI_Booklet_English_CMYK.pdf) (January 2025) sets the adult limit at under 5% of total energy, and warns that even home-made food turns unhealthy when made with high fat, sugar or salt. A sugar-free barfi swimming in ghee still fails that test.

## 5 sugar-free Diwali sweets to make at home, and what sweetens each

Each recipe below is original to this post and makes about 12 pieces or 4 bowls. Every entry lists the same four things in the same order, and quantities are home-kitchen amounts, not lab-tested nutrition values.

### 1. Anjeer-akhrot rolls

- **Sweetened by:** 10 dried figs (about 150 g), soaked 30 minutes; no sugar or jaggery.
- **Base:** 1 cup chopped walnuts, 2 tablespoons desiccated coconut, a pinch of cardamom.
- **Method:** blend the figs coarse, cook 4 minutes in 1 teaspoon ghee, fold in walnuts, roll a log, chill an hour, slice into 12.
- **The catch:** drying concentrates the fig's own sugar, so one slice is one sweet.

### 2. Kesar makhana kheer

- **Sweetened by:** sucralose or stevia, stirred in after the pan is off the heat.
- **Base:** 2 cups roasted makhana, crushed, in 750 ml toned milk with saffron and 8 chopped almonds.
- **Method:** simmer about 20 minutes until thick, cool 5 minutes, sweeten, serve in 4 bowls.
- **The catch:** milk carries its own lactose, and a sweetener sachet must carry the FSSAI warnings below.

### 3. Paneer-coconut sandesh

- **Sweetened by:** 4 soft dates, pureed, plus 2 drops of rose water.
- **Base:** 200 g fresh paneer or chhena, kneaded smooth, with 3 tablespoons grated coconut.
- **Method:** warm the paneer and date paste on low heat for 3 minutes, knead, press into 12 moulds, top with pistachio.
- **The catch:** chhena spoils quickly, so make it on 28 or 29 October and refrigerate it.

### 4. Roasted chana-peanut laddoo

- **Sweetened by:** 6 dates, chopped very fine, and nothing else.
- **Base:** 1 cup roasted chana (dalia) and half a cup of roasted peanuts, ground coarse, with 2 tablespoons warm ghee.
- **Method:** pulse until the mix holds when pressed, then roll 12 laddoos while warm.
- **The catch:** peanuts and ghee make these calorie-dense, so two is already a large serving.

### 5. Ragi-almond squares

- **Sweetened by:** an erythritol or stevia blend, measured by the packet's sugar-equivalent guide.
- **Base:** 1 cup ragi flour roasted in 2 tablespoons ghee, half a cup of almond meal, a splash of milk.
- **Method:** cook into a stiff dough for 6 to 8 minutes, press into a greased tray, cut 12 squares.
- **The catch:** ICMR-INDIAB-21 found that swapping refined cereals for whole wheat or millet flour without cutting total carbohydrate was not linked to lower diabetes risk (odds ratio 0.94, interval crossing 1).

## Jaggery, dates, sucralose or polyols: how the sweeteners compare

The table compares four ways to sweeten a Diwali sweet, plus one option that is not food, using the sources cited here. The last row is SubhSandesh's own data, measured 24 September 2026.

| Sweetener | Added sugar in ICMR-INDIAB-21? | What the cited evidence says | FSSAI warning on a package |
|---|---|---|---|
| White sugar, jaggery, honey, palm sugar | Yes, all four | ICMR-NIN: under 5% of daily energy for adults | None specific to sugar |
| Whole dates or figs | No, but their fruit sugar remains | WHO (May 2023) names fruit's natural sugars as one way to cut free sugars | None specific |
| Sucralose, stevia, aspartame, acesulfame K | No | Indian trial, 210 adults: no HbA1c change in 12 weeks, 0.5 kg weight loss | Sweetener named; child, pregnancy or phenylketonuria lines by type |
| Polyols such as sorbitol, maltitol, erythritol | No | Outside WHO's 2023 sweetener guideline | "Polyols may have laxative effect" at 10% or more |
| A Diwali greeting page instead of a box | 0 g sugar | 48.3% of SubhSandesh pages opened on a phone; 11.1 views per page | Not a food |

The takeaway: jaggery and honey are not swaps at all, dates are a portion question, and sucralose was neutral for blood glucose in the one Indian trial cited here. Change the base before you change the sweetener.

## What a packaged sugar-free mithai box must say under FSSAI rules

FSSAI's [Labelling and Display Regulations compendium](https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Compendium_Labelling_Display_23_09_2021.pdf) (version of 23 September 2021) requires boxed warnings on any package containing a permitted artificial or non-nutritive sweetener. Read the rectangular box on the back, because the front only says "sugar-free". The required lines include:

- The name of the sweetener, for example "This contains sucralose".
- "Not recommended for children" with saccharin; children, pregnant and lactating mothers with acesulfame potassium.
- For aspartame: not for phenylketonurics, children with seizure disorders, or pregnant and lactating mothers.
- "Polyols may have laxative effect" when a food has 10% or more polyols.
- For 10% or more sorbitol: laxative effect, bloating and diarrhoea in children, and reduced calcium absorption in post-menopausal women.

A loose sweet weighed out at the counter carries none of these lines, so ask the shop what sweetened it. If the answer is jaggery, it is not sugar-free by the ICMR-INDIAB definition.

## What an Indian sucralose trial and WHO's 2023 guideline found

The best Indian evidence on a straight swap is a [12-week randomised trial by Mohan and colleagues](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC11330421) in Diabetes Therapy (24 July 2024). It replaced about 60 kcal of sugar in the tea or coffee of 210 adults with type 2 diabetes with sucralose. HbA1c, fasting glucose and lipids did not change, while weight fell 0.5 kg and waist 0.8 cm.

The [WHO guideline announcement of 15 May 2023](https://www.who.int/news/item/15-05-2023-who-advises-not-to-use-non-sugar-sweeteners-for-weight-control-in-newly-released-guideline) conditionally recommends against non-sugar sweeteners for weight control. It excludes people with pre-existing diabetes and does not cover polyols; for everyone else, WHO's advice is to reduce the sweetness of the diet altogether.

The [RSSDI-ESI clinical practice recommendations (2020)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC7328526) say artificial sweeteners may be consumed in recommended amounts, and name festivals as a reason for regular glucose monitoring in India. So a sucralose kheer suits a person with diabetes; for the rest of the family, a smaller, less sweet serving is the better swap.

## A five-day Diwali plan for someone with diabetes, 27 to 31 October 2027

Diwali 2027 runs from Dhanteras on Wednesday 27 October to Bhai Dooj on Sunday 31 October, with Lakshmi Puja on Friday 29 October. This is a planning list, not medical advice, so check every step with your doctor.

- **Before 27 October:** ask your doctor how many sweet servings fit the week and whether extra glucose checks make sense.
- **Thursday 28 October:** make one batch only, the sandesh or the kheer, so a known sweet waits in the fridge.
- **Friday 29 October:** take prasad as a token piece, then have your own sweet with the evening meal, not as a snack between visits.
- **Saturday 30 October:** carry a small box of anjeer-akhrot rolls when visiting for Govardhan Puja.
- **Sunday 31 October:** for Bhai Dooj, give the sugar-free batch to the sibling who also watches their sugar.

## When a sugar-free sweet is the wrong gift, and where SubhSandesh fits

A sugar-free sweet loses when a doctor has set a strict carbohydrate limit, because date laddoos still carry sugar and ghee-rich barfi still carries fat. It can also read as a remark about someone's health if they never asked for it.

SubhSandesh does not make sweets, and no page replaces a plate shared at the table. The [interactive Happy Diwali card on SubhSandesh](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) ends with a box of mithai opening onto a Shubh Deepavali card signed by you, and lets you name their favourite sweet. People also leave it late: 49.4% of Raksha Bandhan 2026 pages were built on the festival day itself (Raksha Bandhan 2026 data used as the nearest festival analogue, n = 89).

For a partner cutting sugar this Diwali, a [digital bouquet page](https://subhsandesh.in/bouquet-gf) is a sweet gesture with no sugar in it; it is a romance template, not a Diwali one. Neither page suits someone without a smartphone, and neither tastes of anything.

The PLAN phenomenon names ICMR/IDF guidance and the task prompt named IDF/ADA. No IDF or ADA page was fetched and verified within the 3-search budget, so neither is cited; ICMR-NIN, ICMR-INDIAB-21, WHO (2023) and RSSDI-ESI (2020, India's diabetes society guideline) carry the health guidance instead.

The full ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines 2024 PDF (nin.res.in/dietaryguidelines/pdfjs/locale/DGI07052024P.pdf) returned 404 on 2026-10-22; the English DGI booklet (PDF dated 27 Jan 2025) was used for the <5% energy line.

FSSAI's per-category sweetener limits for Indian sweets (Food Additives compendium, 883 pages) were not verified line by line and are not stated.

The sucralose RCT tested tea and coffee, not mithai; the post says so. The Diwali-specific glycaemic study found (Int J Diabetes Dev Ctries 2015, doi:10.1007/s13410-015-0427-8) is paywalled and not in Europe PMC, so it is not cited.
